name: John Tyler
summary: A Virginia states' rights Democrat-turned-Whig, Tyler opposed a national bank, federal internal improvements and high protective tariffs, and defended slavery. As president he vetoed Whig bank and tariff bills, pursued Texas annexation and later backed Virginia's secession.

booksNotUsed.reason: His annual messages were read in the Miller Center dataset (same texts); they only add topics already covered there.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: As senator he voted against the 1828 protective tariff amendments, but as president he sought moderate duties for revenue with 'incidental protection' and signed a tariff in 1842; his record points both ways.

people-in-arms.rationale: He held that a regular staff and enough men to garrison fortifications must be kept in peacetime while the militia is the main reliance, so he did not want the professional army replaced.

taxation-theft.rationale: He said a wise constituency will submit to necessary burdens and urged taxes to meet deficits rather than debt, treating taxation as legitimate.

consent-of-governed.rationale: His inaugural describes the government as deriving its powers from the consent of the governed and having only the power necessary for its operation.

separated-powers.rationale: As senator he voted to censure Jackson for assuming powers not conferred by the Constitution and against the President's protest, backing congressional checks on the executive.

right-to-secede.rationale: After the 1861 peace efforts failed he became a leading proponent of southern secession and was elected to the Confederate House.

territorial-expansion.rationale: As president he negotiated the Texas annexation treaty, urged annexation by joint resolution and signed it in March 1845.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: He was a slave owner and as a congressman voted against prohibiting slavery in Missouri, a record contrary to equal legal rights for all people.

remove-indigenous-peoples.rationale: As president he directed efforts to persuade the remaining Florida Seminoles to remove west, and as senator voted against amendments requiring treaty guarantees before Indian removal.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: His Florida policy sought the removal of the remaining Seminoles from their lands, and he voted against amendments securing tribal rights before removal.

no-central-bank.rationale: He vetoed the Bank of the United States twice and as senator voted against rechartering it and against overriding Jackson's veto, a consistent record against a national bank.

notes: Searched themes: economy (bank, tariff, land distribution, taxes), government (vetoes, executive power, separation of powers, secession), world (Texas, Hawaii, China, Oregon, slave trade), society (slavery, Indian removal), defence (army, militia, navy). Sources were the Miller Center presidential speeches dataset, Voteview roll calls and Miller Center essays; the Congressional Record before 1873 is not in the local corpora, so his Senate speeches were not read. The record is thin for most statements, so many answers are null and the uncertainty rule is expected to fail.
